claims.text: Pack-cementation aluminizing deposits a thin, uniform, aluminum-rich surface layer on the RHEA.
The added aluminum preferentially oxidizes at high temperature to form a continuous Al2O3 scale.
The alumina scale will be dense and adherent.
A dense, continuous alumina scale limits oxygen diffusion and ingress into the RHEA substrate.
The alumina scale grows slowly under the specified high-temperature conditions.
The alumina scale maintains its integrity under thermal cycling.
Untreated structural RHEAs typically do not form continuous protective oxide scales during high-temperature exposure.
Untreated RHEAs form non-protective or poorly adherent oxide scales at high temperatures.
Non-protective or poorly adherent oxide scales cause accelerated oxidation and degradation of the untreated alloy.
Aluminizing will reduce oxidation-related weight gain relative to the untreated RHEA during exposure at 1200°C in ambient air.
Aluminizing will reduce oxide-scale spallation relative to the untreated RHEA under the specified exposure.
The target oxidation-rate reduction is at least approximately 50% under the specified conditions.
The proposed operating condition is approximately 1200°C in ambient air containing about 0.21 atm oxygen for approximately 100 hours.
The expected benefit depends on the aluminizing treatment parameters and compatibility of the treatment with the substrate microstructure.
Oxygen pressures or temperatures outside the stated boundary may produce different oxidation behavior.
Failure to achieve an approximately 50% reduction in oxidation weight gain together with improved scale adherence relative to untreated controls would falsify the hypothesis.
